text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Late profit-taking and origin sales at the highs knocked robusta coffee futures in London from their peaks which saw benchmark May rising at one stage by nearly 10 per cent. May stood at $1,560 a tonne at the finish, still a $50 gain on the day, but well below its ceiling of $1,655. Trading in London was volatile and profit-taking set in as New York retreated from an advance in late US morning trade. London's volatility was further compounded by the fact that many players were increasingly taking short-term view on the market. Arabica futures in New York ended mainly firmer in rollercoaster dealings, but a round of speculative profit-taking pushed prices down from fresh life-of-contract highs set earlier in the day. Most active May coffee rose 0.10 cents/lb on the day, to end at 166.40 cents/lb, after peaking at a new contract high of 173.00 cents/lb. PORTUGAL - Coffee imports in October 1996 amounted to 72,273 bags, up from last year's 56,544 bags. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1996 (January/October) up to 621,351 bags, 20.5 per cent up on imports in the like period the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1995 amounted to 629,621 bags compared to 663,813 bags in 1994. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Brazil (79,500 vs 72,000 bags), Ivory Coast (96,000 vs 70,900 bags), Uganda (56,500 vs 61,100 bags) and Cameroon (50,700 vs 45,700 bags). The major supplier of roast and ground in January/October 1996 was Spain with 30,900 vs 34,600 bags. Coffee exports in January/October 1996 amounted to 80,597 bags, almost 35 per cent up on the tonnage exported in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995 reached 73,994 bags compared to 52,054 bags in 1994. Portugal exports most of its coffee in the form of roast and ground with Spain (56,600 vs 50,200 bags) being the main market

CYPRUS - Coffee imports in September 1996 reached 6,311 bags, which brought cumulative imports in the first three quarters of 1996 (January/September) up to 34,282 bags against 32,650 bags in January/September 1995. Total imports in 1995 reached 48,097 bags against 50,748 bags in 1994. The major supplier of green coffee in January/September 1996 was Brazil with 24,200 bags, up from 9,800 bags in the like period the previous year.
